mechanism_narrative: Consistent quarterly growth in real GDP (GDPC1) signals strong economic expansion, leading to higher corporate earnings and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: GDPC1 growth rate in the prior quarter is positive but S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of such instances.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) exceeds 5.5% for two consecutive months, it indicates a weakening labor market that reduces consumer spending confidence, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: UNRATE remains above 5.5% for two months but S&P 500 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of such cases.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in both payroll employment (PAYEMS) and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) indicates a labor market contraction that reduces consumer spending, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint decline in PAYEMS and UNRATE occurs but S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances.

mechanism_narrative: During a monetary tightening cycle (FEDFUNDS > 2.5% and rising), the Federal Reserve's policy shift increases discount rates, reducing equity valuations and causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: In periods where FEDFUNDS exceeds 2.5% and is rising, S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in industrial production (INDPRO) indicates robust manufacturing activity, boosting corporate profits and driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: INDPRO growth in the prior month is positive but S&P 500 5-day returns are negative in more than 60% of such instances.

mechanism_narrative: When the core inflation rate (CPIAUCSL) exceeds 2.5% annually, it signals persistent inflation that prompts the Federal Reserve to tighten policy, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: CPIAUCSL annualized rate above 2.5% but S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion (HOUST above 1000 thousand units and rising), housing market strength signals robust consumer spending, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: HOUST exceeds 1000 and is rising but S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of instances.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) indicates strong consumer demand, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: HOUST and RSAFS both rise but S&P 500 5-day returns are negative in more than 60% of such cases.
